newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRs sag on rate fears.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRs sag on rate fears.

text.p: American Depositary Receipts (ADRS) sagged on Monday, hurt in part by fears of higher U.S. interest rates.
Decliners led advancers by 412 to 124 among 806 ADRs. The overall index declined 0.98 percent and volume was 39 million shares in early afternoon.
Traders said ADRs, along with U.S. stocks, were hurt by the prospect that the U.S. central bank would raise interest rates at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"The feeling on the Street it that the rate move is going to be up," a trader said. "You're not going to get any more down rates."
Another said, "It's very drifty and there's no massive volume."
Latin American ADRs, which are sensitive to U.S. rate moves, moved generally lower. Brazilian bellwether Telebras fell 3-7/8 to 104-7/8.
British shares also were also weighed by Prime Minister John Major's decision to hold elections May 1, with British Petroleum falling 1-1/2 to 134.
